headline: Imposed $1,000 fines on Wine World, JD's Variety and Unified Petroleum for tobacco sales to a minor.

Office of the 
  
Board of Health 
City Hall 
718 Main Street 
Fitchburg, Massachusetts 01420 
978-829-1870 
 
This was a regular meeting of the Board of Health held in the Legislative Building at 700 Main 
Street and recorded by FATV Studios, Thursday, August 6, 2026.  The meeting was called to 
order by Dr. Bogdasarian.    
 
Present:  Stephen Curry, Director; Dr. John Bogdasarian, Chair; Dianne Tousignant, Board 
Member; Jamie Darcangelo, Board Member; Karen Membrino, Clerk Stenographer; Alexandra 
Nudler, Food & Milk Inspector.  
 
Call to Order:  Meeting was called to order at 4:00pm by Dr. Bogdasarian.  Dr. Bogdasarian 
opened the meeting and explained the purpose of the hearing, the rights of all parties, and the 
procedures to be followed.  
 
New Appointment:  Food & Milk Inspector Alexandra Nudler 
 
Dr. Bogdasarian introduced Ms. Nudler, the newly appointed Food and Milk Inspector for the 
City of Fitchburg.   
 
The Board was informed that Ms. Nudler has been with the department for three weeks and 
holds a Public Health degree from Framingham State University.  Her prior professional 
experience includes an internship with the Westford Health Department and employment as a 
Regional Health Inspector with the South-Central Massachusetts Partnership for Public Health. 
 
Ms. Nudler experience includes food establishments, housing, recreational camps, lake testing, 
and body art, with particular emphasis on food establishments and food trucks. 
 
The Board and staff welcomed Ms. Nudler and acknowledged her work to date, including 
routine inspections, assistance with new establishments, and participation in community 
events. 
 
Requested Hearings:  Tobacco Sales to Minors 
 
1. Wine World, 318 John Fitch Hgway., Saurabh Patel; Selling a tobacco product to a 
person under the Minimum Legal Sales Age; First Violation:  $1000 fine and Tobacco 
Sales Permit suspension of three (3) consecutive business days.
Joan Hamlett, Tobacco Control Agent appeared virtually, and presented the details of the visit 
to the establishment, to the Board.   
 
The Board was advised that on June 19, 2026, at approximately 4:05pm., a 19-year-old trained 
youth inspector purchased ZYN nicotine pouches from the establishment for approximately 
$7.79.   
 
This constituted the establishment’s first youth tobacco-sale violation within the applicable 36-
month period.  Staff reported no prior history of sales to minors in the available database, other 
than educational warnings and one older FDA violation. 
 
Ms. Hamlett recommended a finding of responsibility, imposition of the mandatory $1,000 fine, 
and reduction of the permit suspension to one day, with the remaining two days continued 
pending no further violations within 36 months. 
 
Mr. Patel appeared before the Board and acknowledged the sale.  He explained that his sister-
in-law, who was trained, was stocking the establishment and that the transaction occurred 
while she was rushed.  Mr. Patel stated that he had operated the location for 14 years and had 
been in business in Fitchburg for 23 years without prior underage tobacco or liquor violations.  
He requested leniency based upon his compliance history and the potential impact upon the 
business. 
 
Following discussion, the Board found the retailer responsible for the violation. 
 
Dr. Bogdasarian made a motion to impose the mandatory $1,000 fine and reduced the permit 
suspension to one day.  Motion was 2nd by Jamie Darcangelo.  All were in favor, motion carried.   
Mr. Patel selected Friday, August 28, 2026, as the suspension date.  A hearing decision letter 
will  be issued. 
 
2.  JD’s Variety, 259 Franklin Road., Himanshu Patel; Selling a tobacco product to a 
person under the Minimum Legal Sales Age; First Violation:  $1000 fine and Tobacco 
Sales Permit suspension of three (3) consecutive business days. 
 
Ms.  Hamlett presented the matter to the Board. 
 
The Board was advised that on June 19, 2026, at approximately 12:30 pm., a 19-year-old 
trained youth inspector purchased ZYN nicotine pouches without being asked to provide 
identification.   
 
Ms. Hamlett stated that the establishment had an excellent compliance history, with only one 
sale since 2006, none in the last 9-10 years.  Ms. Hamlett recommended a finding of 
responsibility, imposition of the $1,000 fine, and the reduction of the suspension to one day.
Mr. Patel appeared before the Board, clarified that he purchased the business in October 2013, 
and accepted responsibility.  He explained the circumstances surrounding the transaction, 
including equipment issues and concerns regarding his mother’s health.  He requested 
minimization of the penalty. 
 
Dr. Bogdasarian made a motion to impose the mandatory $1,000 fine and reduced the permit 
suspension to one day.  Motion was 2nd by Diane Tousignant.  All were in favor, motion carried.  
Mr. Patel selected August 28, 2026, as the suspension date.  
 
3. Unified Petroleum, 249 Kimball St, Mr. Kasim; Selling a tobacco product to a person 
under the Minimum Legal Sales Age; First Violation:  $1000 fine and Tobacco Sales 
Permit suspension of three (3) consecutive business days. 
 
Ms.  Hamlett presented the matter to the Board. 
 
The Board was advised that on June 19, 2026, at approximately 1:04pm., a 19-year-old trained 
youth inspector purchased ZYN nicotine pouches for approximately $6.85 without being asked 
to provide identification.  
 
Ms. Hamlett reported that the establishment had an excellent compliance history and no DOR, 
Federal, or State violations during the relevant period.  The last reported sale at the location 
occurred in 2013. 
 
The Board was advised that the owner and manager had previously met with Tobacco Control 
staff regarding corrective measures, including enhanced point-of-sale scanning requiring entry 
of the customer’s date of birth. 
 
Mr. Kasim appeared before the Board and acknowledged the sale by the manager.  He stated 
that he did not wish to terminate the employee and requested leniency.  He confirmed that 
identification checks were standard practice and that scanning equipment has been installed at 
both locations. 
 
Dr. Bogdasarian made a motion to impose the mandatory $1,000 fine and reduced the permit 
suspension to one day.  Motion was 2nd by Diane Tousignant.  All were in favor, motion carried.  
Mr. Kasim selected August 14, 2026, as the suspension date.  
 
Meeting Minutes: 
 
I. Review and Approve meeting minutes of July 2, 2026. 
 
Diane Tousignant made a motion to approve the July 2, 2026.  Motion was 2nd by Jamie 
Darcangelo.   All were in favor, motion carried.
Discussion:  Developing a sustainable trash collection and disposal program 
 
Director Curry provided an update concerning the Waste Reduction Committee’s work.   
The Board was advised that Mayor Squailia has tasked the department with identifying 
potential revenue-generating and cost-reduction measures in response the budget shortfalls in 
regards to rubbish collection and disposal.  The committee includes Councilors, representatives 
of the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection, the Mayor’s staff, the City 
Auditor, a school representative, and Health department staff.  The committee has met 
approximately four times.   
 
The current collection system was reviewed, including trash collection for one-to-eight-unit 
buildings by E.L. Harvey using 64-gallon carts and recycling collection by Waste Management 
every other week pursuant to the Landfill Solid Waste Contract. 
 
Annual collection costs were reported at approximately $1.7 million, with disposal costs of 
approximately $800,00, for a total of $2.5 million. 
 
The Board discussed the Fitchburg/Westminster Landfill, including disposal rates, host fees, 
remaining capacity, and anticipated future operations.  The Board was advised that closure of 
the landfill could result in substantially increased costs due to the loss of host fees and 
increased disposal and transportation expenses. 
 
Additional issues discussed included recycling contamination, food waste and organics, pay-as-
you-throw programs, recycling education, composting and organics programs, grant 
opportunities, potential partnerships, and enforcement of illegal dumping. 
 
Director Curry also stated that legal review indicated that the Board possesses authority 
concerning the proposed program; however, existing City ordinances would require 
amendment of Ordinances by the City Council. 
 
A plan is targeted for presentation to the City Council in mid-September, with possible 
implementation of a new program at the end of this fiscal year.  The Committee may consider a 
lower initial bag fee in order to phase in the new program. 
 
The Board also discussed available State grants, enforcement mechanisms, RFID and serial-
number tracking, multi-family registration, and public education. 
 
Board members asked questions concerning host fees, Landfill ownership and location, landfill 
capacity, recycling markets, and education. 
 
The next Waste Reduction Committee meeting was meeting August 17, 2026 at 11:00am. At 
City Hall, third floor.
Announcements: 
  
1.  10th Annual Community Health Resource Fair – September 24, 2026, from 4:00pm-
6:00pm at the Fitchburg Armory, 14 Wallace Ave. 
 
2. Mosquito Control/West Nile Virus – Mosquito spraying was scheduled for the evening of 
August 6, 2026, in the Canton St and St. Andrew Street areas following detection of two 
positive mosquitos.  Information concerning affected areas, exclusions, and service 
requests were provided through the City Webpage, FATV, social media and Central 
Massachusetts Mosquito Control Project resources. 
 
Other Business/Future Agenda Items: 
 
The Board discussed pending regulations, including Kratom, Septic Regulations, and Animal 
Keeping Regulations. 
 
The Board expressed interest in addressing Kratom regulations at a future meeting, preferably 
after Labor Day weekend to allow for broader public participation.  A special meeting or 
adjustment of the meeting date, including the possibility of September 10 was discussed, 
subject to further consideration and monitoring of State and / or Federal developments. 
 
The next Board of Health meeting is tentatively scheduled for September 3, 2026.   
 
Dr. Bogdasarian motioned to adjourn.   All were in favor.  Meeting adjourned at 5:45PM.
